paras: The police shooting of William Watkins took place in Lynchburg, Virginia, late on the night of August 12, 1910, when Policeman Kelly shot Watkins, a Black man, as he tried to escape arrest on a charge of snatching a white woman's purse. Watkins was first reported dying, but he survived, was jailed, and was sent on to the grand jury for highway robbery. Only Virginia white papers reported the case, all from the police side.
According to the Lynchburg reports, a purse was snatched from Mrs. J. H. Poole, a white woman, as she sat in front of her home on Twelfth Street. The police identified Watkins as the thief.

The Newport News Daily Press said Watkins was located after a long chase and that Kelly fired with his revolver as he tried to run. The bullet struck Watkins in the back, and he was taken to the City Hospital. The same paper added, without giving a source, that Watkins "admitted the robbery." On August 13 the Richmond Times-Dispatch's correspondent wrote that he was "probably mortally wounded" and "can hardly survive."

Watkins recovered enough to be discharged from the City Hospital, and by August 20 he was in the city jail awaiting trial for highway robbery. On September 2 Mayor Smith, sitting in Police Court, sent him on to the grand jury. No report of any inquiry into the shooting itself, or of the outcome of Watkins's trial, was found.

The shooting appeared on August 14 in two Virginia papers, the Richmond Times-Dispatch under "Purse-Snatcher Shot by Officer" and the Newport News Daily Press under "Policeman Shoots Negro." Both treated the theft and the flight as established and gave no account from Watkins or any other witness to the shooting. The Richmond Virginian followed the case in two short items, "Alleged Robber in Jail" and "Wounded Negro Sent on to Grand Jury," the second of which printed his name as "Will Atkins." No Black-press coverage of the shooting was found.

The first reports expected Watkins to die, but later items show he left the hospital for jail. The Richmond Virginian dated the shooting "10 days" before August 20, while the Lynchburg dispatches of August 13 placed it on the previous night.

reader.title: Police shooting of William Watkins
bases: A Lynchburg policeman shot a Black man he was pursuing for arrest; no crowd or mob is reported (A1, A2).

Two separately worded Lynchburg reports of Aug. 13 agree on the shooting by Policeman Kelly, and two later Richmond Virginian items confirm the wounded man's jailing and referral to the grand jury (A1, A2, A3, A4); all accounts give the police side only.

accounts.label: Police account (Lynchburg dispatches)
accounts.gist: Watkins snatched Mrs. Poole's purse, was found after a long chase, and was shot in the back by Policeman Kelly as he ran to elude arrest; he was said to have admitted the robbery.

framing.detail: Lynchburg reports headlined 'Purse-Snatcher Shot by Officer' and 'Policeman Shoots Negro' presented the theft and the flight as fact and the shooting as part of an arrest.
Brief Richmond Virginian follow-ups, 'Alleged Robber in Jail' and 'Wounded Negro Sent on to Grand Jury', tracked his case through the courts.
